source: That branch of the lake of Como which extends southwards between two unbroken chains of mountains, and is all bays and gulfs as the mountains advance and recede, narrows down at one point into the form of a river, between a promontory on one side and a wide shore on the other; and the bridge which here links the two banks seems to emphasize this transformation, and to mark the point at which the lake ends and the Adda begins, only to become a lake once more where the banks draw farther apart again, letting the water broaden out and expand into new gulfs and bays. The country bordering the lake, formed by the deposits of three great torrents, is backed by two neighbouring mountains, one called San Martino, and the other, in the Lombard dialect, the Resegone, from its saw-like row of peaks; so that on first seeing it — so long as it is in profile — looking northwards, for instance, from the ramparts of Milan — one can pick it out at once, on the name alone, from the vast and lengthy range of other mountains of obscurer name and more ordinary form. For a considerable stretch the country rises slowly and continuously; then it breaks up into little hills and valleys and into steep and level tracts, following the structure of the two mountains and the erosion of the water. The shore itself, intersected by the beds of torrents, is almost entirely gravel and pebbles; the rest is fields and vineyards, and scattered towns, villages and farms, with here and there a wood extending right on up the mountain-side. Lecco, which is the largest of these towns and gives its name to the district, lies on the lakeside not far from the bridge, and is even apt to find itself partly in the lake when this is high; it is a big town nowadays, well on the way to becoming a city. At the time of the events which we are about to describe, this township which was already of some importance, was also fortified, and so had the honour of housing a commandant and the advantage of a permanent garrison of Spanish soldiers, who taught modesty to the wives and daughters of the town, tickled up the shoulders of an occasional husband and father, and, towards the end of summer, never failed to scatter themselves among the vineyards, to thin out the grapes and lighten the labours of the vintage for the peasants. Paths and tracks used to run — and still do — from one to another of these villages, from the mountain heights to the lakeside, and from one precipice to the other. Sometimes they run steep, sometimes level, and often drop suddenly and bury themselves between two walls, from which, when one looks up, only a patch of sky and some mountain peak can be discerned. Sometimes they come out on open terraces; thence the eye ranges over prospects of varying extent, always full of interest and always changing, as each point of vantage takes in different aspects of the vast landscape, and as one part or the other is foreshortened, or stands out, or disappears. One can see a piece here, another there, and then again a long stretch of that great varied mirror of the water; on this side the lake is shut in at one end, or rather lost among the ins and outs and groupings of the mountains, then spreads out again between more mountains, unfolding one by one, and reflected upside down in the water with the villages on the shores; on the other side is more river, then lake, then river again, losing itself in a shining coil among the mountains, which follow it, getting smaller and smaller until they too are almost lost in the horizon. The very spot from which so many different views can be seen itself appears in views from every side. The mountain on whose foothills you are walking unfolds its cliffs and pinnacles above and around you, each standing out on its own and changing at every step, turning what had just seemed a single ridge into a whole series of ridges, and showing on a height something that a moment before had seemed down on the shore; the quiet and cosy character of these foothills pleasantly tempers the wildness around, and is a foil for the grandeur of the rest of the landscape.

rows.text:
The island rose that morning, which the fishermen called their debtor, where the patrol boats taught their lessons of rescue to those who had paid already with everything they owned, and the radar swept its arcs as if counting souls for mercy, and the holding pens waited with their curriculum of patience. The coast guard cutter, whose hull bore the blue stripes that marked it a classroom of confinement, began to toil through the grey swells in order to harvest the living from the water before the living could reach the land they had been told was sanctuary, and to sort them into categories that the officers wrote on forms that the officers called by names that meant nothing to the sorted, and to wait until the lawyers could decide which names meant freedom and which meant return, so that the island might remain what the ministers in their offices far north had promised it would be: a place of instruction, a place of waiting, a place of not-yet.

The waves that broke against the cliffs, which the old maps had drawn as mere notation, which the new maps shaded in bureaucratic pink, which the satellite rendered each hour into grids of watchable colour, seemed to speak in a language the listening devices strained to parse. The wind rose and fell; the light changed; the hours passed.

The boats came in the dark and in the grey, and the lights moved across the water.

The camp stood on the hill, which had been a military post before it became a place of temporary receiving, and the fences ran down to the harbor, and the harbor ran out to the horizon that no fence could reach.

The officers filed their reports, which the translators rendered into languages the officers did not speak, and the sea kept its own records in salt and drift, and the names changed when the forms were stamped, so that a man who had boarded as passenger became, in the interval of ink drying, something the regulations called by a term that meant he could be moved, or held, or returned, depending on which office held the form.

The thermographic camera, which detected heat before it detected faces, showed the arriving bodies as blooms of temperature against the colder water, and the screen in the command room rendered them as numbers that crept across the grid, and the operator watched, and the operator spoke, and the boats turned, and the boats arrived, and the men who stepped from them shivered, and the men who stepped from them were told to wait, so that the island might process what the sea had delivered, and the night might end, and the dawn might bring its own instructions.

The procedures continued. The water rose and fell.

The instructions were read, and the interpreters listened, and the forms were filled, and the buses waited, and the planes waited, and the sea continued.

The holding area filled, and emptied, and filled again, and the coordinates were logged, and the vessels were tracked, and the drownings were recorded in a separate column, and the recoveries were recorded in a column adjacent, so that the arithmetic of the operation might be visible to those who read only numbers.

The morning we write this, the patterns continue: the detection and the interception, the classification and the removal, the water that receives what the land refuses. The island remains, which Europe calls its southernmost point, where the temperature of compassion is measured in milliseconds of decision, and the grammar of rescue has learned to conjugate itself through conditional clauses that lead always to the same shore, and the waiting continues, and the waves repeat their lessons, and the horizon stays where it has always been: visible, unreachable, necessary.

The vessel that patrols these waters, which the Ministry of Interior designates a platform for rescue and humanitarian instruction, maintains its station where the African current meets the limestone shelf, because the thermal gradient draws shoals upward at dawn and because the radar signature of an inflatable degrades in salt haze, and it lingers there to harvest those who would otherwise vanish, a practice the logbooks term *salvage* though the holding bays below deck receive them already shackled, the officers having learned to apply the cuffs before the cameras wake, before the journalists on the aft deck finish their coffee, before anyone might testify that the men were compliant, that they rose from the gunwales with their palms open, that they asked only for water and for the coordinates to be radioed ahead, so that their families might know they had not drowned, so that the debt collectors might wait another season, so that the village they left might imagine them still living, still sending, still becoming the ones who return with engines and with roofs.

The skiff that founders at the thirty-fifth parallel, which the pilots call the threshold of responsibility, which the lawyers parse as the outer edge of contiguous jurisdiction, which the thermal cameras render as a bloom of orange against the black, demands to be read as an event without precedent, as though each hull had not already split along the same seam, as though the waterline were not already mapped, as though the nameless were not already named in the database that grows in a server farm outside Palermo, and the waves rise, and the hull settles, and the children are lifted last, as protocol requires, as mercy dictates, as the manual prescribes.

The island rises from the sea in bays and inlets, in coves and in shallows.

The lighthouse that the navy automated in 1985, which the fishermen still call by the name of the keeper who drowned, stands where the limestone shears away.

The sea swallows and the sea releases; the sea dilates across the horizon until the eye invents a shore, then contracts to the hull's own shadow, then swells again to meet the aircraft descending from the north, and at the coordinate where the territorial water ends and the contiguous zone begins, the same body of water changes designation without changing color, without changing temperature, without any instrument but the document that declares it so, the line invisible except to the satellite, except to the treaty, except to the judge who will later read the coordinates aloud.

The screen that displays the incoming craft, which the operator watches without touching, which the algorithm has already flagged as probable noncompliant, shows also the reflection of the operator's own face, and the face appears inverted, and the face appears older than the operator knows himself to be, and the craft appears closer than the telemetry confirms, and the gap between image and object yawns, and the gap between object and policy yawns wider, and the operator learns to trust the screen, and the operator learns to doubt the screen, and the operator waits for the command that will authorize the approach, and the command arrives, and the command does not arrive, and the hours pass in this rhythm of readiness and deferral.

The syntax of this vigilance undulates: it swells with clauses, it subsides to fragments, it crests again in the long periodic sentence that mirrors the long periodic wait, the prose itself *lapping* at the shore it describes, lapping in advance of the landing that the narrative must yet unfold.

The rescue swimmer trains to enter the water without splash, to surface without gasp, to become the element that receives the element, and the training continues.

The holding center that processes the arrivals, which the regulations term a facility for identification and orientation, which the inhabitants call the warehouse, which the lawyers call the site of systemic delay, stands on the road that climbs from the harbor, and the buses ascend, and the buses descend, and the buses sometimes wait for hours with their engines running, and the heat accumulates, and the forms accumulate, and the present tense of this description—this accumulation, this waiting, this running—extends now into the present of your reading, into the present of my writing, into the present that has not yet resolved what it will become.

The island that rises from the African current, which the fishermen have long called the gate of tears, bears on its eastern flank a cove where the patrol vessels moor while the thermal cameras scan the horizon because the wakes of wooden boats dissolve before the optics can resolve them and the algorithms must learn to read desperation as a statistical anomaly, to interpret thirst as a calibration error, to classify the living as cargo; and the officers who stand on the pier, whose grandfathers fished these waters for tuna, have been taught to call the interception a rescue even when the hulls are swamped by their own wake, to term the detention reception even as the steel gates lock behind the disembarked, to name the forced return voluntary departure, a lesson they repeat each dawn without irony, without the vocabulary for what they witness, as the instructors from the mainland arrive to refine these protocols, to help them see the drowning as administrative failure, the dead as data points to be entered before the shift ends, before the light changes and the next flotilla appears where the continental shelf drops away and the color of the water shifts from turquoise to the blue that admits no bottom, no purchase for the eye.

The cliffs that guard the southern approach, which the geological surveys date to the Miocene, which the erosion maps predict will crumble within two centuries, which the pilots use as their first landmark when the mist lifts, seem to wait in a patience older than record, while the buoys mark the limit beyond which the jurisdiction pauses, while the satellite dishes track the orbits that define this pause, while the lawyers in Strasbourg debate whether the pause constitutes a sea.

The tide withdraws and the tide returns.

The lighthouse keeper, who has watched this reciprocation for thirty years, who has learned to read the weather in the behavior of the gulls, speaks of it to no one.

The currents here, which the maritime charts render in arrows of graduated blue, which the rescue manuals warn will carry a swimmer beyond hope in twenty minutes, which the smugglers exploit because they must, contract and dilate according to pressures the barometers barely register, according to gradients invisible until the surface itself betrays them with a line of foam, a sudden stillness where the water heaps against its own resistance, then releases, spreads, opens corridors through which the desperate navigate by stars they learned in villages that no longer exist, by phones whose batteries die in the second night, by the sound of helicopters that sometimes means salvation and sometimes means surveillance, the same sound carrying both possibilities until the moment of distinction, until the document is produced, the stamp, the radioed code that transforms the encounter from one category to another without changing the salt on the skin, the thirst, the angle of the sun.

The radar screen in the operations room, which reflects the actual disposition of vessels as pulses of green light, which represents this disposition as a grid of coordinates, which translates the coordinates into assignments for the fleet, doubles the sea: there is the sea that slaps against the hulls, and there is the sea that glows in the darkened room where the duty officer watches for the signature of an unregistered mass, for the pattern that means overcrowding, for the absence of transponder that means fear, and the two seas correspond and invert, the glowing one contracting as the actual one dilates with dawn, the actual one contracting into the terror of the hold while the glowing one dilates into the abstraction of arcs and vectors, the medium of this doubling being neither water nor light but the electromagnetic pulse that names itself in its return, that calls the thing it touches by the name of its echo.

The night passes. The dawn comes.

The fishermen, who set their nets before first light, who have found bodies in the mesh, who have learned not to speak of this in the harbor bars, who maintain nonetheless a ledger of the unnamed, haul and rest, haul and rest, the rhythm of their labor undulating against the rhythm of the patrols, against the rhythm of the arrivals that peaks with the calm of August and subsides with the winter storms, the three waves not synchronized but interlocking, each trough containing the crest of another, so that the island itself seems to breathe in three time signatures, the geological, the seasonal, the catastrophic, and the prose that would describe this must likewise rise and swell and fall and gather and release, must coil through its own periods in a motion that prefigures the crossing it narrates, the word *traverse* naming at once the migrant's passage, the sentence's sinuous advance, and the narrative's promise of arrival that the text will withhold, will defer, will suspend in the condition of approach.

Now, as I write this, the wind has shifted to the sirocco and the forecast speaks of another surge.

The coastguard cutter that patrols the corridor where vessels founder, whose humanitarian mission the radio logs term "rescue," because the lexicon of intervention must borrow from sanctuary even where the impulse is to interdict, and because the protocols name every boarding a "salvage," though the holds contain only the expelled, steers through waters that swell and constrict, to swell again, as if the sea itself were learning respiration.

The horizon that the watch-keeper scans, which the radar screen translates into luminous geometry, which the thermal imager renders as zones of relative warmth, because the body in water marks a heat-signature against the colder element, shows nothing; yet the protocols require the search to continue, for the interval between sighting and retrieval must be compressed, because survival is measured in the minutes that elapse before hypothermia claims what dehydration has spared.

The waves rise and fall.

The island that the cutter circumscribes, which the charts designate a port of first arrival, looms.

The beacon that marks the anchorage, whose automated flash the lookout recognizes, and whose intermittent signal the log records, governs a zone where territorial waters end and the contiguous zone begins, where the same water changes jurisdiction according to instruments held on shore, because the line itself is imperceptible, though its consequences are not.

The hull that cleaves the passage, whose wake the moonlight silvered, whose engines the silence magnified, and whose course the current deflected, held steady; and the reflection that the surface offered, which the glass inverted, because the medium of water preserves the image but reverses the vertical, showed the stars below as the stars above showed themselves, and the depth that the sounding measured, which the chart corroborated, and the hazard that the marker indicated, which the pilot noted, to disregard, to commit to memory, threatened.

The crew must rest.

The watch that relieved them, because the regulations prescribe rotation, because fatigue impairs judgment, and the vigilance that the darkness demanded, because the running lights of small craft are visible only at distances too short for evasion, and the tension that the interval between detections generated, because absence of signal is not signal of absence, maintained.

The dawn that the eastward glass announced, which the colorimeter would have quantified as shift in wavelength, which the eye received as gradation from black to grey to rose, because the atmosphere scatters light according to its thickness, revealed the sea's expansion, its surface extending to the curvature of the earth, then its contraction, as the first heat raised mist from the cooler water, then its re-expansion, as the sun burned through, because the diurnal cycle governs visibility as the seasonal governs traffic.

The migrants that the binoculars found, whose vessel the surge had half-swamped, whose movements the distance reduced to semaphore without code, whose number the estimate would later dispute, because the capacity of the cutter is fixed and the arithmetic of selection is unwritten, waited; and the approach that the coxswain executed, which the training had rendered automatic, which the conditions made hazardous, because the swell and the debris and the panic of the boarded create a geometry of risk, required the helmsman to hold, to adjust, to hold again.

The transfer that the protocol mandated, because the island's facilities are designated, because the mainland's are distant, because the regulation distinguishes between rescue and landing, completed.

The documentation that the officer completed, which the database would receive, which the periodic report would aggregate, because the institution requires the singular to be rendered as instance of type, recorded what the body could not speak, and the silence that the processing imposed, because the questions must be answered before counsel is provided, because the timeline of asylum is not the timeline of need, enclosed.

The shore that the cutter regained, whose breakwater the morning light transformed from barrier to threshold, and whose infrastructure the funding cycles had expanded and constricted, according to calculations made elsewhere, because the pressure of arrival is measured against the tolerance of electorates, received them.

The island that the fishermen call Lampedusa, which rises from waters that have swallowed more prayers than the churches of any mainland, lies where the African plate grinds beneath the European, and where the charities that style themselves rescue missions ply their trade of interception and return, because the drowning must be managed, because the living must be taught the lesson of the threshold, and because the accounts must balance, which the administrators who draft the memoranda that govern the patrol boats that scan the horizons where the inflatables founder understand as well as they understand the sonar that maps the trenches where the cold currents run, which is to say: with the patience of men who have learned to call containment by the name of salvation, to call the holding cell a place of safety, to call the forced embarkation a voluntary departure, and to call the sea itself, when it swells between two jurisdictions, by the name of no-man's-land, which no map recognizes and no court adjudicates, yet which every ledger records, every spreadsheet tracks, every audit confirms, as the waves swell and subside, as the contracts swell and subsides, as the moral credit of the operation swells and subsides, in the troughs and crests that the passage itself now begins to trace, to heave, to swell toward what the syntax prefigures and the narrative must unfold.

The waters that surround it, which the pilots know by their rips and calms, which the thermographers read by their temperature signatures, which the algorithms parse for anomaly and distress, hold in their depths the archives of those who did not arrive, whose names the databases preserve in fields the living cannot query, whose silence the reports note as statistical residue, as the margin of error, as the cost of doing business, because the sea is a ledger that accepts no appeal, because the wind is a jurisdiction that recognizes no flag, because the night is a courtroom where no advocate speaks, and yet the operations continue, the patrols continue, the transfers continue, as the moon continues, as the tide continues, as the debt continues, in the rhythm that the prose now takes up, that the meter now insinuates, that the ear now catches: the slow iambic pulse beneath the administrative diction, the ten-syllable wave that rises and falls, that carries the sentence forward, that buries its own music in the overt sense, as the patrol boats bury their wakes, as the radar buries its frequencies, as the state buries its intentions in the passive constructions of the press release.

The island swells and the island subsides, and the night comes down upon it, and the patrols depart from it.

The lights that mark the harbor, which the captains read for entry, flash their intervals of invitation and warning, and the dark that surrounds them, and the dark that they punctuate.

The sea that morning, which the meteorologists had predicted would moderate, which the duty officers had hoped would permit the scheduled transfer, contracted in the dawn hours to a surface almost glass, a membrane stretched between two regimes of visibility, because the calm is also a condition, because the flatness is also a text, because the document that records the weather records also the decision to sail, and the decision to sail records also the liability, and the liability records also the indemnity, and the indemnity records also the renewal of the contract, which names the sea by one name in its first clause and by another in its annex, which marks the boundary not by coordinate but by instrument, by the paper that the captain carries, by the stamp that the official applies, by the fax that the office confirms, so that the same water, undifferentiated to any eye, becomes by this operation territorial and then extraterritorial, becomes by this operation subject to rescue and then to return, becomes by this operation visible to law and then invisible to law, in the dilation and contraction that the passage now runs through, in the expansion of the claim and the constriction of the claim, in the full arc that the duality demands and receives.

The horizon that the watchkeeper scans, which the binoculars frame and the screen supplements, doubles in the lens of the equipment that records it, inverts in the display that transmits it, transforms in the compression that stores it, because the image is also a witness, because the file is also a deposition, because the archive is also a tribunal, and the patrol that the watchkeeper observes, and the inflatable that the patrol observes, and the bodies that the inflatable carries, which the patrol will intercept, which the patrol will board, which the patrol will redirect, and the forms that the patrol will complete, and the signatures that the forms will require, and the handovers that the signatures will enable, and the returns that the handovers will effect, and the silences that the returns will produce, and the silences that the silences will compound, until the operation closes upon itself, until the file closes upon itself, until the narrative closes upon itself, in the specularity that the structure now installs, in the mirroring that the medium now names.

The patrol departs and the patrol returns.

The documentation to complete, the evidence to preserve, the account to render, and the watch to resume, and the horizon to scan, because the cycle is continuous, because the sea is patient, because the debt is never discharged.

The night falls and the operations cease, and the operations resume, and the radar sweeps, and the infrared detects, and the coordinates fix, and the vessels converge, and the interceptions multiply, and the transfers accelerate, and the returns compound, in the coordination that the syntax now layers, in the accumulation that the grammar now permits, in the density that the period now achieves.

The island remains, which the geology calls recent, which the history calls strategic, which the policy calls externalized.

The dawn that the passage now approaches, which the narrative has promised, which the syntax has prepared, which the proleptic word has marked in its own body of swelling and subsiding, of heaving and settling, of the wave that is both water and sentence, both scene and medium, both present and future, rises now upon waters that the present of writing still troubles, that the present of writing still records, that the present of writing still witnesses, because the description is never complete, because the operation is never final, because the sea, which this sentence now releases, which this syntax now lets fall, continues beyond the period, beyond the paragraph, beyond the page, in the continuity that the form has encoded, in the persistence that the structure has ensured, in the return that the beginning always was.

The patrol vessels that thread the shipping lanes south of Malta, which the European agency calls its corridor of humanitarian vigilance, drift where the thermal currents rise and the radar clutter thins, and they wait, as the watch officers have learned to wait, for the hulls that show no running lights, for the inflatables that sag in the swells, for the bodies that sometimes surface at dawn without the documents that would name them, without the stamps that would mark them as having passed through any jurisdiction, as having been counted, as having been seen; and the crews, who rotate through four-month deployments that the service terms rest cycles, learn to read the sea's two languages, the one of dilation that lifts the eye toward the empty horizon and the one of contraction that pulls it down to the oil slicks, the debris fields, the coordinates where the last signal registered before silence, before the satellite trace dissolved into the database's archival fog, before the case file migrated from the operational queue to the closed ledger, where it rests now, where it rests still, where it rests until the next inquiry, the next audit, the next parliamentary question that will demand the notation be reopened, be reexamined, be reclassified according to the protocols that the directive establishes, that the regulation mandates, that the implementing decision renders binding upon all member states, upon all agencies, upon all vessels operating under the flag or the charter or the memorandum of understanding that the ministry signs, that the cabinet approves, that the parliament ratifies in the session we are writing in, in the month we are writing in, in the year that sees the arrivals rise again, that sees the drownings rise again, that sees the same sea perform its same indifference.

The boats that the shipyard at Porto Empedocle builds for the mission, which the tender specifies as high-endurance interceptors, which the crew manual describes as semi-displacement hulls optimized for boarding operations, which the budget line item records as maritime security assets, which the inventory tags as Sector South deployable, await their commissioning in the yards where the cranes lift and the welders seal and the painters spray the grey that will mark them as belonging to the fleet, as belonging to the operation, as belonging to the space that the map shades in two tones, the operational and the reserved, the active and the standby, the zones where the rules of engagement apply and the zones where they suspend, where they lapse, where they await reactivation upon the order that the command structure issues, that the political authority validates, that the situation on the ground, on the water, in the air, demands.

The night falls, and the heat rises, and the radio crackles.

The island that the pilots approach from the north, which the charts mark as Lampedusa, which the fishermen knew before the charts, which the currents shaped before the fishermen, sits where the African shelf drops and the deep water begins.

The watch officer who the night vision reveals as standing at the rail, who the thermal imager shows as searching the dark, who the logbook will record as having sighted nothing, having logged nothing, having transmitted nothing, stares into the black that the instruments parse and the black that the instruments miss, and he waits, as they all wait, for the shape that will resolve from the clutter, for the contact that will validate the sweep, for the confirmation that will permit the approach, the hail, the boarding, the transfer to the protocol that the directive establishes for intercepted persons, for rescued persons, for persons whose status the preliminary assessment cannot determine, whose status the subsequent interview will clarify, whose status the appeals procedure will test, whose status the final determination will fix, will seal, will archive in the file that the system generates, that the database stores, that the retention schedule eventually deletes.

The radar that the mast carries, which the manufacturer warrants for forty nautical miles, which the maintenance contract covers through the fiscal year, which the spare-parts inventory supports, which the training module simulates, sweeps its arc and returns its echoes, and the operator reads them, and the operator doubts them, and the operator confirms them with the glass that the bridge keeps ready, with the binos that the SOP requires, with the mark-one eyeball that the slang still honors, that the slang still invokes, that the slang still contrasts with the screens, with the feeds, with the synthetic displays that overlay the world with its own ghost, with its own double, with its own image that the lens captures, that the sensor processes, that the algorithm annotates, that the analyst reviews, that the report incorporates, that the briefing presents, that the decision-maker consults, that the archive preserves, that the historian will query, will parse, will read against the grain of its own pretense to transparency, to immediacy, to the unmediated real.

The engine starts, and the hull cuts, and the wake spreads.

The course that the navigation plotter sets, which the waypoints define, which the exclusion zones constrain, which the traffic separation schemes channel, which the environmental regulations protect, leads through waters that expand and contract, that the chart names as open sea and the experience names as confinement, as exposure, as the medium that offers no purchase, no shelter, no mark by which to orient the self that the journey has dissolved, that the journey has reconstituted, that the journey has delivered to the threshold where the name changes, where the status changes, where the document that the officer holds, that the officer presents, that the officer stamps, declares the crossing complete, declares the crossing interrupted, declares the crossing suspended in the juridical void that the instrument creates, that the instrument names, that the instrument renders legible as a gap, as a hiatus, as the space between the departure recorded and the arrival not yet granted.

The horizon that the dawn reveals, which the light flattens, which the haze obscures, which the mirage doubles, which the longing misreads, shows first the single hull, then the second, then the constellation that the rescue coordinator counts, that the rescue coordinator plots, that the rescue coordinator assigns to the assets that the network maintains, that the network activates, that the network deploys according to the availability that the real-time display shows, that the real-time display updates, that the real-time display renders as a field of vectors, as a field of velocities, as a field of probable intersections that the algorithm calculates, that the algorithm refines, that the algorithm presents as the optimal solution, as the efficient allocation, as the humanitarian calculus that the press release celebrates, that the annual report highlights, that the audit questions, that the litigation tests, that the judgment we are awaiting, that the judgment we are writing toward, will confirm or will dissolve.

The swell lifts, and the swell drops, and the rhythm continues.

The deck that the morning finds wet, that the salt crusts, that the sun bleaches, that the crew hoses, that the crew swabs, that the crew maintains in the state of readiness that the inspection requires, that the inspection verifies, that the inspection documents in the form that the administration prescribes, in the format that the administration validates, in the system that the administration accesses, bears the marks of the traffic it has seen, of the hands it has received, of the bodies it has counted, of the bodies it has failed to count, of the bodies that the sea has taken before the deck could receive them, before the crew could reach them, before the protocol could engage, before the jurisdiction could assert its claim, its responsibility, its burden that the law assigns, that the law distributes, that the law we are interpreting, that the law we are applying, will determine to have been met or to have been breached.

The wind turns, and the current shifts, and the island changes aspect.

The operation that the headquarters names as active, that the field commander names as ongoing, that the participant names as endless, that the survivor names as the threshold, as the ordeal, as the passage that memory will fix and memory will distort, that memory will transmit in the fragments that the interview captures, that the case file records, that the evidentiary standard admits, unfolds in the time that the log timestamps, that the GPS track spatializes, that the narrative will reconstruct, will dramatize, will reduce to the arc that the genre demands: the departure, the crisis, the rescue, the landing, the processing, the determination, the outcome that the statistics aggregate, that the policy debates, that the election decides, that the history judges, that the archive preserves in the silence of its own completeness, its own closure, its own claim to have said all that can be said, all that need be said, all that the saying exhausts.

The heat shimmers, and the distance wavers, and the coast approaches.

The patrol vessel *Dignity* steams through waters that the European Maritime Safety Agency designates as humanitarian corridors, which the Libyan Coast Guard interprets as spheres of sovereign extraction, while the swell heaves and settles, while the radar sweeps and sleeps, and the watch officer notes coordinates that the satellite renders as algorithmic care, intending to mark for rescue those whom the same spectral gaze has already catalogued for interception, the rescue itself becoming instruction to wait, to drift, to hope for hulls that will come before thirst unbinds the tongue from its last mooring, before the body surrenders its archives to the salt.

The waves that morning rose like breath drawn slow and held, like the held breath of those who wait for names to be called, like the names that wait on lists whose sequence the wind rearranges, and the light fell clear enough to read by, clear enough to read the water's texture, clear enough to see what the water would not keep.

The hulls came in hulls and hulks.

The first boat that season carried forty-three, whose bodies the coroner would count as forty-three, whose bodies the state would enumerate as arrivals.

The thermal camera distinguishes those who move from those who do not, and to move is to survive by the instrument's logic, and to survive is to become visible to the logic that distributes visibility, and the officers train daily in the recognition of distress, in the simulation of drowning, in the calibration of response times that the protocol names as adequate, as humane, as meeting the threshold of non-refoulement that the court in Strasbourg has found the threshold to be, the sea itself having no threshold, the sea having only this surface where the expanded and the contracted meet, where the swell that morning had promised breadth, had opened its blue to the horizon's invitation, and then the mist came down, and the blue contracted to the boat's own dimension, and then the wind shifted, and the dimension opened again toward some elsewhere the compass could not hold, and the legal point of interception lay twelve nautical miles from a coast that the chart named as territorial and the current named as elsewhere, the distinction held only in the document that the Libyan signatory had not yet ratified, had initialed in Tripoli while the same water moved under other designations.

The officer observes; the screen observes the officer observing; the algorithm observes the screen and flags anomaly; and the anomaly is a vessel, and the vessel is a pattern, and the pattern is a threat or a victim, and the threat is victim to the same taxonomy, and the taxonomy breathes, and the taxonomy ceases to breathe, and the officer must decide before the breath ceases what name the pattern wears, what response the name requires, and the training has taught the hesitation that saves, the training has taught the hesitation that costs.

The waves rose. The protocol rose to meet them.

To read the water is to learn its refusals, is to note how the parallax corrects itself, how the horizon rights its own distortion, how the instruments that measure depth also measure their own uncertainty, and the depth here is three thousand meters, and the uncertainty is complete, and the complete record will note coordinates and time and wind speed and the number of souls and the number of bodies and the discrepancy between these numbers that the investigation will not close.

The night brought vessels. The vessels brought night.

The swell that had carried the morning's clarity now carried darkness visible only as absence on the screen, as the negative space where signal should be, as the interruption that the system logs and the watch reads and the hand writes in the ledger that the morning watch will read, and the reading will not say what the darkness held, what bodies the darkness passed through, what names the darkness dissolved, and the dissolution itself is logged as meteorological, as condition, as force majeure, as the sea's own jurisprudence.

The morning found the *Dignity* where the night had left her, and the night had left her searching, and the searching had found the empty and the full, the hull that rode high and the hull that rode low, the high hull empty of all but the residue of presence, the low hull full of water and of what water fills, and the distinction between these hulls was the distinction the morning made, the morning that now rose clear, that now contracted to mist, that now expanded to the full reach of a visibility that found nothing to see, that found the sea empty as the ledger's promise, as the protocol's prediction, as the training's assurance that to look is to find, that to find is to save, that to save is to return, and the return is to Libya, is to the coast that the document names as safe, is to the safety that the names on the lists will not recognize, that the bodies in the ledger will not inhabit, that the sea in its waviness prefigures already, the wave that gathers, the wave that breaks, the wave that gathers again.

The island that watches the southern approaches, which the fishermen who ply its harbours call simply the rock, rises where the currents meet, as the morning light gathers and as the night fog settles, and the vessels gather, whose hulls carry no names that register in the ports of departure, to await the signal that will send them onward, that will send them back, that will send them where the documents say they must go, to be processed, to be held, to be returned, to be lost in the registers that no hand retrieves.

The waves that break upon its eastern shore, which the oldest charts mark as the gate, which the newer instruments read as a zone, which the patrols themselves have learned to call by numbers only, seem to breathe with the tide; the swell mounts, the swell falls; the hours pass as hours pass; the light changes; nothing is concluded.

The wind rises and falls.

The boats appear, which the watchers have learned to spot at the rim of sight, and they vanish, which the same watchers record in logs they do not keep.

The sea that surrounds the anchorage, which swells and contracts according to pressures no instrument on the island measures, seems to open and to close, to offer passage and to deny it, to remember and to forget what passes through it, to hold and to release, governed by instruments that float in orbits no eye traces, that mark where jurisdiction begins and where it simply continues, as if the line were drawn in water, as if the water were not already elsewhere.

The horizon that the tower surveys, which the glass renders as a line one might touch, shows what the glass does not show: the same line reversed, the same touch denied, the vessels doubled, the vessels singular, the vessels present, the vessels removed, the vessels held in the medium that preserves them only by inverting them, by making them signs of themselves, by making them wait, by making them wait longer, by making them wait until the waiting itself becomes the record they keep of having been here.

The light shifts; the depths alter.

The operations continue, to monitor, to interdict, to classify, to transfer, to detain, to return, to save, to count, to forget, as the present hour writes what the present hour will not read back.

The coordination holds: the rescue and the prevention, the shelter and the exclusion, the care and the constraint, the identification and the erasure, proceed as one motion, as one policy, as one hand that opens and closes, that opens what it has closed, that closes what, by another name, it opened, the name changing where the document changes, the document changing where the water does not, the water continuing as the water continues.

The archives accumulate, which the officers who compile them call memory, which the officers who consult them call intelligence, which the officers who transmit them call cooperation, which the officers who receive them call burden, which the officers who delete them call discretion, and the deletions themselves are archived, and the archives of deletions are deleted, and the pattern holds, and the pattern is broken, and the pattern holds again, as the syntax of the operation swells and subsides, as the sentences of the operation lengthen and shorten, as the waves of the operation mount and fall, and the word that names this mounting and falling, that names the prose that records it, that names what the record itself will become, is the word the passage keeps for what comes after, the word that folds the watching into the watched, the recording into the recorded, the border into what crosses it, the sea into what the sea receives.

The island rises from waters that the maritime patrols, who circle it with instruments of rescue they call humanitarian, have charted as a zone of preemptive interception, where vessels that drift in currents and in darkness, swelling and subsiding in the thermal rhythms of the sea, wait for those who would claim them as sanctuary to gather them back into the architecture of refusal, a structure designed to teach the waters safety by denying them shore, to instruct the horizon in modesty by drawing its limits closer, to tutor the wind in navigation by binding it to channels where it must carry documents that rename what it moves across, so that the same stretch of water, when a bearing is taken and a coordinate fixed, ceases to be passage and becomes, by the stroke of an instrument, jurisdiction, and then, when the record closes, becomes passage again, and those who move through it find themselves, in bays and inlets where the light pools and withdraws, learning the curriculum of the state.

The vessel that the radar tracks, which the thermal imaging renders as a bloom of signatures, which the acoustic array triangulates into a pattern of breathing, moves through a medium that the protocols designate as liquid barrier and liquid bridge, and the night is warm, and the engines drone, and the holding pattern tightens.

The waves break and the hulls rise.

The craft that the surveillance network registers, which the database timestamps, approaches a threshold that the agreements define as rescue and as return.

The officers who the manifests identify, who the rotations assign to this sector, deploy the tools that the manuals describe as protection and as deterrence, to intercept the bodies that the currents deliver and the policies disperse, and the sea that the morning light reveals, which the satellite captures and the archive stores, offers to the lens a surface that mirrors and inverts, so that the horizon that the eye perceives and the sensor records carries the image upside-down, and the vessel that approaches and the vessel that waits exchange positions in the reflection, and the operation that the directives authorize, which the reports consolidate, proceeds through phases that the schedules mark as assessment and as transfer, and the holding facilities that the contracts establish, which the inspections validate, expand and contract in cycles that the budgets regulate and the protests interrupt, and the sea that the same light traverses, now measured and now unmeasured, receives the name that the document bestows and loses it when the document closes.

The patrols depart.

The island that the maps fix, which the erosion alters, which the storms reshape, presents to the view a profile that the guides describe and the photographs reproduce, and the limestone that the quarries extracted, and the dust that the winds distribute.

The horizon that the dawn clears, which the haze obscures, which the noon flattens to a line, draws the eye outward and the policy inward, and the depths that the soundings plumb, and the shallows that the tides expose, and the currents that the buoys mark, and the rips that the warnings name, and the color that the depth changes, and the color that the sediment changes.

The operation that this hour, as I write, continues to unfold, transforms the water into a field of simultaneous rescue and prevention, and the same vessel that the previous watch designated as target becomes, in the next watch's notation, evidence.

The heat that the asphalt gathers, which the thermometers record, distorts the air above the landing zone, and the rotors that the schedules require, and the fuel that the tenders deliver, and the crews that the rotations exhaust, and the noise that the residents protest, and the dust that settles and rises, and the pattern that the flights inscribe, which the radar preserves and the analysts study, creates a grammar of approach and delay, of promise and deferral, that the bodies below must learn to read in vibration and shadow, and the sea that the same heat flattens, which the same light penetrates and scatters, offers no single depth but a stratification of visibilities, where the surface that the eye reads and the surface that the instrument reads diverge, and the vessel that one register confirms and the other suspends occupies two conditions at once, until the document that the protocol requires resolves the contradiction by naming, and the name, once fixed, travels through channels that the agreements establish and the disputes unsettle, and the same stretch of water, in inlets and bays where the light pools and withdraws, receives and loses its designation according to the phase of the operation, and the phase of the operation advances according to the availability of the name, and the name, when it arrives, carries with it the whole architecture of before and after, of here and elsewhere, of those who may remain and those who must continue, and the continuation that the currents promise and the policies foreclose unfolds in the interval between the bearing taken and the bearing confirmed, an interval that the prose itself, in its own undulation, measures and crosses, so that the syntax that crests and subsides, that swells with clause upon clause and releases into the short declarative, performs the very movement it describes, the wave that precedes and prepares what the narrative, gathering its own momentum, will unfold.

The watchtower that the coast guard built to shelter those they would later interrogate commands the eastern ridge, where the limestone crumbles into scree that slides and settles, that swells and subsides with each winter's rain, and where the radar technicians who calibrate their instruments to track vessels whose names they will never learn have learned instead to read the phosphorescent bloom of hulls against the phosphorescent bloom of waves, to distinguish between the charitable rescue and the predatory interception, between the pedagogical orientation session and the coercive removal, all while waiting to intercept, to document, to facilitate the safe and voluntary return that no one has ever described as voluntary once the documentation is complete, to assist in the identification of remains that the same documentation will certify as never having arrived, to train others in these same charitable arts, to build the capacity for humane deterrence, to expand the infrastructure of care in order to contract the horizon of arrival, to seal the sea while promising passage, to open the sea while enforcing its closure, to make the sea itself the instrument of selection, the medium in which some are reflected upward toward air and others downward toward the sediment where the limestone keeps its own records of pressure and time.

The vessel that the currents deliver to the anchorage where the mooring chains calcify with each season's accretion of shells and salt, the vessel whose registry the inspectors dispute while the holds still hold what the holds have held, the vessel whose master must declare before he can be permitted to declare anything else, this vessel enters now the jurisdiction that it entered an hour ago when the line was crossed that no instrument can locate except the document that retroactively locates it, the water that was open becoming closed, the water that was closed becoming open, the sea dilating and contracting around a hull that does not change but changes name, that was rescue and becomes interception, that was interception and becomes rescue, depending on which record is consulted, which timestamp is trusted, which witness has survived to testify to the boundary that the water itself does not recognize, that the radar sees only as echo, as return, as the same signal twice, the same hull twice, the same wave twice, the vessel that departs and the vessel that arrives made one in the specular medium of the screen where the technician watches the technician watching.

The tide rises and the tide falls.

The cove that the fishermen abandoned when the regulations changed, that the patrol boats now use for refueling, this cove collects what the currents deliver and the currents withhold.

The detention center that the architects designed to process arrivals in bays and inlets, to sort the swelling from the subsiding, to distinguish between the subsiding and the swelling, this center stands at the point where the asphalt meets the limestone, where the infrastructure meets the foreshore, where the document meets the body it presumes to describe, the same body that the same document will describe differently when the jurisdiction changes, when the timestamp changes, when the witness changes, the body that was in need of protection becoming the body that needs to be deterred, the body that was deterred becoming the body that needs protection, the sea that was open becoming the sea that is closed becoming the sea that is open again, the full arc of expansion and contraction played out in the time it takes to stamp a form, to scan a fingerprint, to determine that the fingerprint has no match in any database that the matcher is permitted to access, to determine that the match exists in a database that the matcher is not permitted to acknowledge, to hold the body in the space between these determinations, in the cove, in the inlet, in the bay, in the space where the water is neither open nor closed but both, where the hull is neither rescued nor intercepted but both, where the technician watches the screen watch the technician.

The lamp that the lighthouse casts across the channel, the lamp that the smugglers use to calibrate their own instruments, the lamp that appears in the binoculars that appear in the painting that hangs in the office where the decisions are made, this lamp doubles and redoubles, the light that is seen and the light that is represented, the light that is represented and the light that is seen, each inversion marked by its medium, the glass, the lens, the pigment, the screen, each transformation leaving its trace in the syntax that describes it, the clause that expands to accommodate the doubling, the clause that contracts to mark the return to singularity, the waviness that is not only in the water but in the grammar that describes the water, in the very structure of attention that follows the wave and follows the wave, that crests with the embedding and troughs with the release, that crests again before the reader has fully descended, the syntax itself a prefiguration of the movement it describes, the movement that the narrative will unfold, the unfolding that the syntax has already performed, the performance that the syntax continues to perform, now, as I write this, as the present of writing punctures the atemporal present of the description, as the limestone that was and is and will be meets the limestone that is being described at this moment, that is being eroded at this moment, that is being built upon at this moment, the watchtower that was completed in the year that I do not name and that is being reinforced in the year that I name by its presence here, now, in this sentence, in this present that is not the present of the waves but the present of their documentation, the present of the radar that returns what it receives, the present of the screen that reflects what it displays, the present of the eye that watches the eye watching, the specular present, the historicized present, the puncture that lets the pressure equalize, that lets the depth be sounded, that lets the syntax breathe before it must submerge again.

The current carries and the current resists.

The horizon that the binoculars bring close, that the smugglers' phones bring closer, that the satellite brings closest, this horizon remains, the dilation that precedes every contraction, the contraction that precedes every dilation, the rhythm that the prose must follow if it is to be true to the water it describes, the water that does not know it is being described, that does not know it is being patrolled, that does not know it is being crossed, that knows only the pressure of depth and the release of surface, the same pressure and release that the syntax enacts, that the reader feels in the length of the periods, in the depth of the embedding, in the return to the simple sentence, the tide rises, the tide falls, the expansion, the contraction, the re-expansion, the full arc, the complete breath, the syntax that waves and waves.
